chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about the disowned son whose father renounces him before the authority, and disclaims his inheritance and his liability. I asked: to whom does his inheritance belong? He said: Ali عليه السلام said, "It belongs to the closest of people to his father."

key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ: the ruling authority before whom the repudiation is made
key_terms.جَرِيرَتِهِ: liability for wrongdoing or financial responsibility connected to his acts
key_terms.لِأَقْرَبِ النَّاسِ إِلَى أَبِيهِ: to the nearest relatives connected to his father

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, who inherits from a disowned son when his father repudiates him before the authority?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a disowned child whose father formally repudiates him before the ruling authority and disclaims both inheritance ties and liability for his acts. The ruling states that the inheritance is assigned to the closest relatives of the father, making it a fiqh report related to inheritance and kinship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5674 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a disowned son (makhlooh) whose father publicly renounces him before the authorities and disclaims both his inheritance and responsibility for his actions.
I asked: "Who inherits from him (the father)?"
Imam (as) replied: "Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled: 'His inheritance goes to the closest relatives of his father.'"
